structured.answer: The page's cheapest choice is an account at Psagot (פסגות) with the fund "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)" no. 5139282: about 86,942 ₪ after 10 years from 10,000 ₪ now plus 500 ₪ a month, assuming 7% a year. But the list shows 86,492 for the same thing, so I'd ask my son before doing anything.

stuck.where: Screen 1 top box vs screen 2 account list
stuck.why: The first box says 86,942 ₪ for Psagot and the list says 86,492 ₪. Same digits, swapped, so I don't know which is right.
Lots of red minus numbers (-447, -1,268, -4,492). I didn't know if they meant losses, and they made me want to back away.
The 7% return was already filled in. Nothing says whether that's sure, and 70,000 growing only to 86,942 doesn't match my idea of 7% a year.
Four crossing coloured lines. I couldn't read it and stopped soon after.

findings.what: The 7% return is filled in already, with no clear warning that it isn't guaranteed
Red minus amounts on almost every fund are frightening and not explained where you see them
Dark background with small grey text is hard to read even enlarged
findings.where: All screens, especially the notes under each bank

findings.what: Too many funds with English names and many coloured tags, a very busy screen
The thin colour bars use oranges and yellows that are too close to tell apart
Jargon everywhere with no Hebrew explanation (קרן מחקה, צוברת, נאמן, מנוטרל מט"ח)
The chart with four crossing lines doesn't say in words what it shows
